html:
Poet, playwright and scholar of New Spain, now Mexico, and a nun of the Order of Saint Jerome. She is the greatest writer of colonial Spanish America.

Born in a village near Mexico City, she learned to read at three and taught herself Latin. As a teenager she served at the viceroy's court, where she impressed a panel of scholars with her learning. With marriage her only other path, she entered a convent in 1669, where she could study. She gathered one of the largest libraries in the colony.

She wrote love poems, plays, religious verse and the long philosophical poem First Dream. Her verses "Foolish men" mock men who blame women for faults that men cause.

In 1690 a bishop published one of her letters with a rebuke telling her to stick to religion. Her reply of 1691 is a famous defence of women's right to learn. Soon after, under pressure from the Church, she gave up her books and writing. She died in 1695 while nursing her sisters during an epidemic.
